title: Writing 'Mood Indigo'
summary: Bigard says Duke wrote the first part and he wrote the other part; it was recorded with his small group, Mills took it, he got $25, and his name came onto it through ASCAP only after 28 years.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well, I suppose this would be as good a time as any to talk about 'Mood Indigo'.
Oh, yeah, 'Mood Indigo'. He said he wrote that while he was having breakfast with his mother.
And actually what happened? I think you told me the story once before, but on this tape -- about 'Mood Indigo'.
Yeah. Yeah, he wrote the first part of
it (humming). He wrote that. But he didn't write the other part (humming). He didn't write that.
You wrote your part first and then he added --
Yeah, he added that part. He did that part. I give him that credit.
You wrote it and I think you told me once that you sold it to him. Is that right?
Yeah. We recorded it and Mills got hold of it, naturally, and then he gave me $25, and just by luck my name got on it, through ASCAP, and that's why I get royalties from it.
But didn't you say that it didn't get on it for a long, long time?
I didn't get on it for the first 28 years.
And there's no way of correcting that.
Well, did you write it for a recording session?
Yeah, we did it for a recording session.
